title: Grits, instant, made with water, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: Grits are finely ground corn kernels designed for quick preparation. This instant version is meant to be cooked with water and a small amount of added fat, making the dish richer and more flavorful. Grits are commonly used as a side dish or a breakfast base.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Grits originated in the Southern United States as a staple of low‑cost cooking.
Instant grits cook in 5‑7 minutes, ideal for busy schedules.
Corn, the base of grits, is rich in carotenoids that give it a yellow hue.
Traditional grits are often served with cheese, butter, or milk.
Grits can be turned into sweet dishes with fruit, honey, or maple syrup.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Grits provide slowly digestible energy, helping to maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Corn fiber supports healthy digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Grits contain thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Iron in grits helps maintain normal hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium contributes to muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn products.

items.title: High sodium in some mixes
items.content: Certain instant grits contain added salt; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Added fat increases caloric density; those watching weight should account for it in their diet.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Bring water to a boil, add the grits and a small amount of fat (butter, cream, or oil). Stir well and simmer for 5‑7 minutes until tender. Season with salt, spices, cheese, or fresh herbs as desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dry instant grits in a cool, dry place, keeping the package tightly sealed. After opening, transfer to an airtight container. Shelf life is indicated on the packaging.
